scope.chapter: Normal Modal Logic — Syntax and Semantics

findings.finding: The negation induction case is guarded by prvFalse, duplicating the falsity case, although its case formula and argument concern not B.
findings.controlling_evidence: The frozen basic-language formation clause and adjacent substitution definition guard negation by prvNot and falsity by prvFalse.
findings.required_translation_handling: Guard only the negation case by prvNot, leave the proof formulas intact, and disclose the tag repair adjacent to the case.

findings.finding: The final equivalence in the negation case converts world non-satisfaction into world satisfaction of a negation, but its justification cites the propositional satisfaction definition.
findings.controlling_evidence: The world-indexed satisfaction definition in the preceding section gives exactly this negation clause; the first step of the proof separately uses propositional satisfaction.
findings.required_translation_handling: Cite the world-indexed model satisfaction definition in that final justification and disclose the corrected citation.

findings.finding: The biconditional induction case begins with B lif C, while the case header, true/true-or-false/false expansion and final substitution formula all use biconditional semantics.
findings.controlling_evidence: The frozen propositional biconditional truth clause and the case's own two-branch expansion require B liff C; the conditional truth clause is handled by the preceding induction case.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace only the first displayed lif by liff in the biconditional case and disclose the repair adjacent to it.
